title: Extensions of smooth unipotent algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $N,E,Q$ be smooth affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:N\hookrightarrow E$ be a closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and let $q:E\to Q$ represent the fppf quotient $E/N$ [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]: $q$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation, and $i$ identifies $N$ with its scheme-theoretic kernel. A smooth affine group is unipotent if it admits a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation, a closed immersion into $\operatorname{GL}_d$, in which every point over every algebraically closed extension is a unipotent matrix, meaning $(g-I_d)^m=0$ for some $m\geq1$ [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. If $N$ and $Q$ are unipotent, then $E$ is unipotent. No connectedness, commutativity, centrality or characteristic-zero hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135, closure of unipotent groups under extensions; the faithful-matrix interpretation is explained in the footnote there and Section 14(c), printed pp.286--287.

proof.text: Choose the faithful matrix representations in the hypotheses for $N$ and $Q$. A closed immersion is injective on points over every commutative $k$-algebra, and the geometric unipotence hypothesis applies in particular over the algebraically closed field $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-unitriangular-embedding] separately to these two smooth affine finite-type groups. We obtain closed embeddings $N\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_a$ and $Q\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_b$ over $k$, with $a,b\geq1$. In the remaining steps a fixed vector always means fixed over every commutative algebra, not just by rational points.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135; Theorem 14.5 and Corollary 14.12, printed pp.281--283, translating the matrix hypothesis to rational-representation unipotence.

proof.text: Let $V\ne0$ be any finite-dimensional rational $E$-module. By [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], use interchangeably its group-scheme representation and its coaction $c_V:V\to V\otimes_k k[E]$. Restrict the representation to $N$ and choose a basis of $V$. The embedding of $N$ from step 1 and [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] give a nonzero $v\in V$ fixed by $N(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Thus its restricted coaction is exactly $v\mapsto v\otimes1$, as required for descent.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135 (nonvanishing of the N-fixed space); Theorem 14.5(b) implies (a), printed pp.281--282; Remark 4.1, printed p.84.

proof.text: The given $q$ represents $E/N$. The quotient of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] and the given $Q$ represent the same fppf sheaf, so their representing isomorphism identifies their quotient maps and kernels. In particular $q$ is faithfully flat in the coordinate-algebra sense. Apply [lem-sfb-central-kernel-cyclic-representation-descent] to $q$, $V$, and $v$. The smallest $E$-subcomodule $W\subseteq V$ containing $v$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional, $N$ acts trivially on it, and its $E$-action is the pullback of a rational $Q$-action. This application requires neither centrality of $N$ nor connectedness of any group.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135; Lemma 5.15 and Theorem 5.13, printed pp.101--102; Proposition 5.25, printed p.105.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] to the descended $Q$-representation on $W$, using $Q\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_b$ from step 1. It gives $0\ne w\in W$ fixed by $Q(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. For each $e\in E(A)$ its action on $W_A$ equals the action of $q_A(e)$, by the pullback identity in step 3. Consequently $w$ is fixed by $E(A)$ for every $A$. Its image in $V$ is nonzero and fixed. We have proved that every nonzero finite-dimensional rational $E$-module has a nonzero rationally fixed vector.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135: the quotient acts on the invariant submodule and supplies a fixed vector.

proof.text: By induction on $d=\dim_k V$, every finite-dimensional rational $E$-module admits a full flag $0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_d=V$ by rational submodules, with trivial action on each $V_j/V_{j-1}$. For $d=0$ the empty flag suffices. If $d>0$, step 4 supplies a nonzero rationally fixed $w$, and $L=kw$ is a trivial one-dimensional submodule. Under [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], its coaction is $w\mapsto w\otimes1$. Therefore $(\pi\otimes1)c_V$, where $\pi:V\to V/L$, vanishes on $L$ and defines a coaction on $V/L$; the counit and coassociativity identities descend from those on $V$. Apply the induction hypothesis to this $(d-1)$-dimensional module. Inverse images of its flag under $\pi$, preceded by $0\subset L$, give the asserted flag. The induced quotient coactions are exactly the trivial coactions from the induction hypothesis. Scalar extension preserves these inclusions and quotients because vector-space exact sequences split linearly.

source.place: Proposition 14.3, printed p.280: finite-dimensional flag argument from the fixed-vector property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-representation-kernel] to the trivial closed normal subgroup of $E$. (It is cut out in $k[E]$ by the augmentation ideal, so its coordinate algebra is $k$.) We obtain $d\geq1$ and $r:E\to\operatorname{GL}_{d,k}$ with trivial scheme-theoretic kernel. For any $k$-algebra $A$, if $r_A(x)=r_A(y)$ then $r_A(y^{-1}x)=I_d$, hence $y^{-1}x=1$ by the stated kernel equality on $A$-points. Thus $r_A$ is injective for every $A$. By [lem-sfb-geometric-unipotence-faithful-closed-immersion], $r$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Corollary 5.19, printed p.103, with the trivial normal subgroup; Corollary 3.35, printed p.75 (equivalently Theorem 4.9, printed p.87).

proof.text: Apply the flag of step 5 to the representation $r$ from step 6 and choose a basis adapted to this flag. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, the matrix of $r_A(e)$ in that basis is upper triangular with all diagonal entries $1$: preservation of $V_j\otimes_k A$ gives the zero entries below the diagonal, and triviality on each rank-one quotient gives the diagonal entries. Therefore $(r_A(e)-I_d)^d=0$, since each multiplication by this strictly upper triangular matrix lowers the flag by one step. In particular this identity holds for every point over every algebraically closed extension of $k$. Changing the basis conjugates the faithful closed immersion by an invertible constant matrix and preserves both closed immersion and nilpotence. This is precisely unipotence in the statement. The argument uses no connectedness or characteristic restriction.

source.place: Proposition 14.3 and Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), printed pp.280--281; Section 6.45, printed p.135.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135; with the matrix/fixed-vector translation and flag argument of Theorem 14.5, Corollary 14.12 and Proposition 14.3, printed pp.280--283.

Supporting representation-theoretic input: Steinberg endomorphisms detect a nonzero fixed vector. Supporting Self-duality of rho section modules at characteristic-dependent weights. Supporting input: Positive-characteristic simplicity step, using irreducibility of the Steinberg induced module rather than assuming self-duality. Numerical input to the dimension comparison: Weyl dimension of the induced module. Supporting Integral Euler character of arbitrary flag line bundles. Section 22d, proof of Theorem 22.50, p.480: general fixed-point input, stated here in its integral equivariant form; Example 22.36, pp.473--474, for formal characters. WANTED: Nielsen 1974 general fixed-point theorem and Iversen 1976, 9.4; neither document is present. The integral formulation is an agent-supplied supporting statement. Geometric input to nonfixed-locus annihilation: invariant affine strata of the reduction, before the Laurent-coefficient and localization arguments. Supporting normal-case neighbourhood input used after passing to the invariant smooth locus, before removing one affine open in the Noetherian induction. Supporting proof input: Linearize the normal quasi-projective neighborhood by an immersion into projective space of a rational representation. Supporting line-bundle prerequisite: replace an ample invertible module by a positive tensor power carrying an algebraic G-linearization, before choosing invariant sections. Supporting Picard input: a tensor exponent uniform over the generic residue fields of all normal components, before applying the generic-line pullback criterion. Supporting base-change input: Brion Lemma 2.3, pullback Pic(G) to Pic(G_K), specialized using Remark 2.2(v). Supporting substep: Brion Lemma 2.3 proof, printed p.118, first three sentences (unipotent radical, affine-space variety and trivial torsor); Remark 2.2(v), p.117, for splitting over an algebraically closed field. Geometric integrality of a connected smooth algebraic group is included explicitly as a structural prerequisite. Supporting lemma: Section 6.45, printed p.135, closure of unipotent groups under extensions; the faithful-matrix interpretation is explained in the footnote there and Section 14(c), printed pp.286--287.

Step 1: the unitriangular-embedding hypotheses hold because closed immersions are injective on R-points, k is algebraically closed, and N and Q are smooth. Step 2: the fixed-vector node applies to the restriction to N; the dictionary formula gives the coaction v⊗1. Step 3: by Yoneda, q is identified with the faithfully flat quotient map of the quotient-geometry node, with kernel N; the descent node explicitly needs no centrality. Step 4: the explicit formula gives r^E_A(e)=r^Q_A(q_A(e)), so w is fixed by E(A). Step 5: the flag induction is genuinely elementary and set up explicitly. Step 6: the kernel node applied to the trivial subgroup plus the all-R injectivity criterion gives a faithful closed immersion. Step 7: in a flag-adapted basis the matrices are unitriangular, so (r-I)^d=0. Edge cases checked: N=E, N=1, finite p-groups, dim V=1. No duplicate in the DAG; no cycle (911-node closure); all citations are in the item's unit, so no tool_uses; no SGA.
